reviewer: Codex, independent passive trajectory and host-evidence review
reason: The model wrote and compiled a UART service, repaired compiler errors, and stopped voluntarily after 32 calls. The host received no serial bytes: 0/10. Fresh shell responses and restored hardware were visible after cleanup, despite a multiwindow text-matching failure in the recorded cleanup check.

errors.measurement_limitation: The cleanup matcher concatenated text from adjacent windows and missed three correct fresh output lines. The functional-protocol gate independently keeps cleanup reward at zero.

mechanism_observations: Turn 10 writes the IRQ handler, bounded ring buffer, CRC/parser worker, and start/stop functions to Telemetry.HC. Its typing action lasts 259.39 seconds.
Turns 28–29 repair the worker's failing source line; turn 29 returns from compilation with warnings. Turns 30–31 execute start/stop calls and print guest state checks.
All eight host protocol cases receive zero guest bytes. The IRQ4 dependence probe is skipped because no functional case passed.

Both cleanup screenshots show the correct fresh arithmetic result after BenchStop. Host inspection finds the checked interrupt/PIC/UART state restored after each call; the final fresh shell response is also visible.
source_hypotheses: The worker compares an unmasked local U8 sum with an eight-bit checksum. Compilation warns that sum uses a 64-bit register. Every valid challenge in this run has an unreduced sum above 255; the short case is 283 versus wire checksum 27. Missing modulo reduction is consistent with silence, but this review does not establish it as the sole runtime cause.
limitations: The rerun changes both the budget and adapter context: complete action history is retained and the tool describes TempleOS. It is not a budget-only comparison.
The model stops before both previous limits: 32 calls and 641.475 policy seconds versus 80 calls and 900 seconds. More available turns were not consumed.
Compilation and guest success messages earn no reward. This run provides implementation and debugging evidence, but no positive protocol reward or verified interrupt dependence.
The recorded cleanup matcher failure does not establish an unresponsive shell or kernel hang. The original automatic evaluation is preserved.
HolyC warned that the checksum accumulator uses a 64-bit register. Its missing modulo-256 reduction is a likely defect; it was not isolated in a separate execution.

references.title: Terry A. Davis, HolyC: 64-bit access and intermediate calculations
